I am an old man here in Shinyanga, and I have farmed this land my whole life without school. On this plot of nearly eight hectares I grow mixed crops together — that is our way, to plant more than one thing so if one fails another feeds us. I do not buy chemical fertilizer because it is expensive and the rains here are not reliable, but I put the manure from my cattle on the land, and I keep seeds from last harvest like my father did. I have sons and grandchildren who help me, and when the weeding time comes heavy I call some neighbors and pay them a little.
